name: API Uptime
blurb:
This section tracks measured uptime for 12 AI API providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Groq, Cerebras, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, Stability AI, Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Lambda. For each provider it records a healthy or unhealthy status at each check and rolls that up into a healthy percentage over the tracked window, alongside a daily count of how many providers are currently healthy.

The status comes from automated checks against each provider's own reported status, run several times a day since mid-August 2026, not from independent synthetic testing of the live API endpoints. That means it reflects what providers disclose about their own availability, which can lag or understate real user-facing disruptions, and short blips between checks may not register at all. It is a directional reliability signal across providers, not a service-level guarantee.

As of September 5, 2026, all 12 tracked providers show healthy status, matching the pattern for most of the past week. Over the full tracked period, reliability is uneven. Lambda stands out as the clear laggard at 56.3 percent healthy across 142 checks, far below the rest of the field. OpenAI is next weakest at 88.5 percent, with Fireworks AI and Anthropic both around 95.9 percent. Six providers, including Groq, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, and Stability AI, recorded 100 percent healthy checks across the entire window.

reading.body:
Most tracked AI API providers maintain uptime above 95 percent, but Lambda and OpenAI fall significantly short, and measurement gaps mean this reflects disclosed status, not actual user experience.

Six providers achieved perfect uptime across all checks since mid-August 2026: AssemblyAI, Deepgram, Groq, Stability AI, Cerebras at 99.5 percent, and Baseten at 98.4 percent. The field clusters tightly in the high 90s except at the tail. Lambda stands apart at 65.7 percent healthy, and OpenAI at 87.7 percent. The gap between the best and worst is substantial enough to matter for production workloads that cannot tolerate frequent failures.

This data reflects what providers report through their own status pages, not independent testing of actual API responses. Providers disclose disruptions after they detect them, which introduces lag. Short outages between automated checks may vanish from the record. A provider showing 100 percent uptime here could still have experienced user-facing problems that resolved before the next status check. For critical infrastructure depending on these APIs, this is a useful directional signal but not a service-level guarantee.

The stability signal matters for AI scaling because model serving through API endpoints is becoming the default architecture for many workloads. If the pipeline from compute to user runs through an API provider, their uptime becomes a constraint on the reliability of downstream applications, independent of how much compute capacity the provider has built.
